# dsh-gemini-oauth-bridge
English | 简体中文
Bridges a **Google AI subscription** (AI Pro / AI Ultra, via the Antigravity / Code Assist OAuth sur
face) into an **OpenAI-compatible endpoint** that DeepSeek Harness (DSH) can use directly as a model
an **OpenAI-compatible endpoint** that DeepSeek Harness (DSH) can use directly as a model provider.
> **Important boundary**: Google AI subscription developer quotas only cover the AI Studio web UI an
d OAuth login inside official CLI tools (Gemini CLI / Antigravity); **API-key usage is billed separa
tely**. This plugin speaks the same OAuth surface as the official client, so it consumes subscriptio
n quota rather than API credit — but that also means it is not a Google-sanctioned third-party integ
ration. Account risk / breakage is possible; evaluate for yourself.
## Features
- **Login and go**: one-click Google OAuth from Settings → Gemini OAuth (authorization code + loopba
ck callback), with automatic `loadCodeAssist` registration / `onboardUser` onboarding and upstream m

odel discovery.
- **OpenAI-compatible endpoint**: `/gemini-oauth-bridge/v1/chat/completions` (stream

ing SSE + non-streaming) and `/v1/models` (so DSH can discover models).
- **Full protocol translatio
n**: system messages, multimodal (data-URL images), function calling (tool_calls ↔ functionCall/func

tionResponse), `reasoning_content` (thinking stream), usage stats, finish-reason mapping.
- **Gemini
3 thought-signature replay**: the server remembers upstream `thoughtSignature` values by tool-call
id and re-attaches them to functionCall parts on the next turn — OpenAI format carries no signatures

, and Gemini 3 multi-turn tool calls fail without replay.
- **Subscription-friendly (anti-drift)**:
dynamically tracks the latest shipping Antigravity client version for the User-Agent (stale versions
are rejected for newer models); requests carry `requestType: "agent"`, a stable derived `sessionId`

, and `agent-<uuid>` request IDs; keep-alive connections without `Connection: close`.
- **429 cooldo
wns**: parses upstream `Retry-After` / `retryDelay`, enters a per-model cooldown window, and refuses

requests locally during it instead of hammering upstream.
- **Catalog honesty**: an entry the upstr
eam catalog flags `disabled: true` — e.g. `gemini-4-argon-disabled` ("Unavailable" / "available to U
ltra and paid Pro plan subscribers") — is never published as a DSH model, so the picker cannot offer
something that can only fail. A request for an id the account cannot use returns the upstream's own
explanation plus a refresh hint instead of an opaque `404 Requested entity was not found`. Per-mode

l context/output limits are read from the upstream `maxTokens` / `maxOutputTokens` fields.

## Install

Restart `dsh --profile web`, then open Settings → **Gemini OAuth**.
## Usage
1. Click **登录 Google 账号** (Log in with Google) and finish the flow in your browser. The plugin tempo
rarily listens on `127.0.0.1:51121` for the loopback callback — this exact redirect URI is registere

d for the Antigravity client and the port cannot change. Port conflicts are reported explicitly.
2.

After login the page shows the account, project ID, tier, and model list.
3. Register the bridge as
a DSH provider in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` (port matches your DSH web URL, default 3080):

### Local state
`~/.dsh/gemini-oauth-bridge.json` (mode 0600, contains OAuth tokens — treat as a secret):
| Field | Meaning |

| `tokens` | access/refresh tokens and expiry |
| `email` / `project` / `tier` | login account and r

egistration result |
| `models` | upstream model cache (refreshable from the UI) |
| `modelCaps` | p

er-model `contextLength` / `maxCompletionTokens` read from the upstream catalog |
[该节后续省略]
## Security
- OAuth tokens live in `~/.dsh/gemini-oauth-bridge.json` (mode 0600) and are never returned by any e

ndpoint; `/api/status` exposes only account metadata (email, project, tier) and the model list.
- DS
H applies a Host/Origin fence to its own `/api/*` routes, but a plugin `webServer.register({kind: 'p
refix'})` route is dispatched before that fence, so the bridge enforces the same rules itself: a req
uest is refused with 403 when its `Host` is not an authority the bridge serves, when `Sec-Fetch-Site
: cross-site`, when `Origin` is the opaque `null` a sandboxed frame sends, when `Origin` disagrees w
ith `Host`, or when a request arrives with no `Host` at all from anything other than a loopback peer
. This blocks DNS-rebinding reads of `/api/status` and `/v1/*`, quota-burning calls through `/v1/cha
t/completions`, and blind-CSRF of the mutating POSTs (`/api/login`, `/api/logout`, `/api/refresh-mod
els`) — a cross-site `Content-Type: text/plain` POST needs no CORS preflight, so without the fence t

he browser would deliver it.
- `/v1/*` is unauthenticated by default because DSH calls it locally; s
et `"apiKey"` in the state file to require `Authorization: Bearer <value>`, and `"trustedHosts": ["h
ost:port"]` to serve DSH on a non-loopback address.
## Limitations
- **Unofficial usage**: relies on the Antigravity client's public OAuth credentials and a non-public
`v1internal` surface; Google may change or restrict it at any time. Intended for individual subscri

bers' own use.
- Single account (no rotation); `http(s)://` image URLs unsupported (data URLs only);

the signature cache is persisted but LRU-evicts past 800 entries.
- The login callback occupies `12

7.0.0.1:51121`; logging in while the Antigravity desktop app is also logging in may conflict.
- Gene
ration goes to the `daily-cloudcode-pa` channel (matching CLIProxyAPI's default); override via `apiC

onfig` if needed.
- **Some catalog models cannot generate.** Upstream advertises entries it will not
serve for your account — the Gemini 4 Argon family appears only as `gemini-4-argon-disabled` with `
disabled: true`, `tagTitle: "Unavailable"` and `tagDescription: "Gemini 4 Argon is currently availab
le to Ultra and paid Pro plan subscribers."`, and every id variant returns `404 NOT_FOUND` even on a
paid `g1-pro-tier` (Google AI Pro) account. Catalog membership is therefore not proof that a model
can generate; the plugin hides `disabled` entries, but no client-side change can enable them.
